what_its_for: Lusutrombopag is used to treat low platelet counts (called thrombocytopenia) in adults who have chronic liver disease and are scheduled to have a medical or dental procedure. Platelets are tiny blood cells that help your blood clot and stop bleeding. This medicine helps your body make more platelets before your procedure to lower your risk of serious bleeding.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Take it at around the same time each day. You will take this medicine for several days before your scheduled procedure. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully about when to start and stop taking it.
dosing: The usual dose is one 3 mg tablet taken by mouth once daily for 7 days. Your doctor will tell you exactly when to start taking it based on the date of your procedure. Do not take more than one tablet per day unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose. Contact your doctor if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original packaging and away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid activities that may increase your risk of bleeding or bruising while your platelet count is still low. Tell all of your doctors and your dentist that you are taking this medicine, especially if you are scheduled for any procedure. Avoid taking blood-thinning medicines like aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen, or warfarin unless your doctor specifically tells you it is safe to do so. Avoid alcohol, as it can worsen liver disease and affect your platelet count.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: unusual or excessive bleeding (from gums, nose, or cuts that won't stop), blood in your urine or stool, severe bruising, coughing or vomiting blood, sudden severe headache, chest pain, shortness of breath, pain or swelling in your arms or legs, or signs of a blood clot such as leg warmth, redness, or swelling. Also contact your doctor if you develop nausea, stomach pain, or yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), as these may be signs of liver problems.
when_it_works: Your platelet count will begin to rise during the 7 days you take this medicine. It usually reaches its highest level around 12 to 15 days after you take your first dose. Your doctor will check your platelet levels with a blood test before your procedure to make sure they are high enough to proceed safely. The effect on platelets will gradually decrease after you stop taking the medicine.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as its safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Older adults (65 years and older) can generally take this medicine at the same dose, but your doctor will monitor you closely. This medicine is not approved for use in children. If you have kidney problems, your doctor should know before you start this medicine, though dose adjustments are generally not required for mild to moderate kidney disease. Since this medicine is used specifically in people with liver disease, your doctor is already aware and will monitor your liver function closely.
